title: Right to Information Act, 2005
facts: Indian citizens have a right to information held by public authorities, subject to the Act.
Public authorities have duties to maintain records and proactively publish specified information.
A citizen can submit an information request to the appropriate public information officer.
Exemptions apply to certain information; the Act also provides an appeals process.

title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
facts: The Act protects consumer interests in relation to goods and services.
Consumer commissions deal with complaints within their legal jurisdiction.
The Central Consumer Protection Authority addresses matters including misleading advertisements.
The Act includes product liability provisions, subject to specified conditions and exceptions.

title: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
facts: The Act provides for free and compulsory elementary education for children aged six to fourteen.
Governments and local authorities have duties relating to access and completion of education.
The Act specifies responsibilities of schools and teachers.
School admission obligations vary by school category and are subject to the Act's provisions.

title: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
facts: The Act empowers the Central Government to protect and improve the environment.
It permits measures to prevent and control environmental pollution.
Industries must comply with applicable standards for emissions and discharges.
Handling hazardous substances requires compliance with prescribed safeguards.

title: Information Technology Act, 2000
facts: The Act gives legal recognition to electronic records subject to its provisions.
It also provides legal recognition for electronic signatures meeting legal requirements.
Unauthorised access and damage to computer resources can attract legal consequences.
The Act addresses identity theft and cheating by personation using computer resources.

title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
facts: The Act provides remedies for women experiencing domestic violence in domestic relationships.
Domestic violence can include physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse.
A magistrate can grant protection and residence orders according to the Act.
Other available relief can include monetary relief, custody and compensation orders.

title: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013
sections: Sections 3, 4, 6, 9, 19; full title includes Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal
facts: The Act prohibits sexual harassment of women at the workplace.
It provides for Internal Committees and Local Committees in the circumstances specified by law.
An aggrieved woman can make a complaint through the process set out in the Act.
Employers have duties including providing a safe working environment and awareness measures.

title: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
facts: The Act protects children below eighteen years from specified sexual offences.
It provides child-friendly procedures for recording statements and conducting proceedings.
The Act sets out reporting obligations concerning offences against children.
Special Courts deal with these cases and must follow the safeguards in the Act.

title: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
facts: The Act recognises rights of persons with disabilities, including equality and dignity.
It includes provisions on non-discrimination and reasonable accommodation.
It sets out duties relating to inclusive education and employment.
Accessibility obligations cover areas including buildings, transport and information under the Act.

title: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
facts: The Act establishes legal services authorities at different levels.
Free legal services are available to eligible persons under the Act.
Eligibility depends on statutory categories and conditions, including applicable income criteria.
The Act provides for Lok Adalats to facilitate settlement of suitable disputes.

title: Indian Contract Act, 1872
facts: The Act sets out general rules governing contracts.
An agreement becomes a contract when the legal requirements for enforceability are met.
Competence of parties, free consent and lawful consideration and object are important requirements.
A breach of contract may give rise to compensation subject to the Act's rules.

title: Copyright Act, 1957
facts: The Act protects specified categories of works including literary, artistic and musical works.
Copyright owners have defined rights such as reproduction, subject to the Act.
Using a protected work without permission can amount to infringement depending on the circumstances.
The Act also provides exceptions, including specified fair dealing uses.

title: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016
facts: The Act regulates real estate projects and promotes transparency in the sector.
Projects covered by the Act must be registered, subject to statutory exemptions.
Promoters have disclosure obligations and allottees have rights and duties.
Aggrieved persons can seek remedies through the procedures provided by the Act.

title: Mental Healthcare Act, 2017
facts: The Act recognises a right to access mental healthcare and treatment under its provisions.
It protects dignity and includes protections against discrimination.
It provides for advance directives and nominated representatives subject to legal procedures.
Confidentiality of mental health information is protected, subject to the Act's exceptions.

title: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
facts: The Act provides for maintenance and welfare of parents and senior citizens.
Eligible parents or senior citizens can seek maintenance under the conditions specified by law.
Maintenance Tribunals consider applications according to the statutory process.
The Act also contains provisions relating to old age homes and medical support.
